content.thinking:
I'm picturing a koala gripping a eucalyptus branch mounted on a wooden base stand, with the branch forking vertically and the koala perched where it splits.

For proportions, I'll scale the koala to roughly 0.7m sitting height, body length around 60-85cm, with a trunk about 1.4m tall and 14cm thick on a round base. I'm deciding the koala should sit at the front of the trunk hugging around it, arms wrapped and legs clasping, with its head turned outward facing the viewer rather than pressed against the bark.

I'm reconsidering the pose — a koala genuinely hugging a trunk would have its face pressed toward the bark, so instead I'll have it perched in a fork with its back resting against the trunk and an arm reaching forward to grip a branch, which reads more naturally and lets the face turn toward the viewer. I'm now laying out the geometry: a base disc, a trunk leaning slightly upward, and an angled branch around 30° from horizontal where the koala will be seated at the fork.

One arm raised gripping near head height, other gripping a thinner twig, legs straddling the seat branch so it passes between them — body upright, back against the trunk for a readable silhouette. I'll have both arms instead wrap backward around the trunk sides, hands meeting behind it, for a more natural hugging pose.

Reworking the arm positions: shoulders placed higher and hands curling around the trunk's sides so fingers are visible from the front, rather than hidden behind. Settling on a sitting koala roughly 0.65 m tall with arms reaching up and sideways to grip the trunk convincingly.

I'll add eucalyptus leaves (bluish-green, lance-shaped) near the koala's face and scattered around, maybe a twig held near its mouth. For the base, a round wooden plinth with radius 0.45 and height 0.08, plus a few fallen leaves and a gum nut resting on it for detail.

For the overall pixel-art style, I'm thinking of using small texel-sized cells (0.02) for fur texture, mostly blocky box shapes but with sweeps for smoother bends in the koala's body and head, keeping sides low-poly (6-8) so the cellPaint texture reads as pixelated. Facial features like the big black nose and eyes will be pixel texture decals layered onto the geometry.

I'm planning the ears as flattened sphere shapes with stepped, staircase-like pixel outlines, grey rims and white fluffy inner cells computed via distance-from-center in each ear's local coordinates. For the skeleton, I'm laying out a hip root, a three-joint spine up to the neck and head, jaw and hinged ears, then arms with shoulder/elbow/wrist joints and simplified hand digits (two thumbs plus three fingers) to approximate a koala's hand structure.

I'm deciding legs need hip, knee, ankle, and toe joints, skipping a tail since koalas don't have one, and folding the branch/stand into the same skeleton under a single "root" joint so everything shares one rig, with stand parts explicitly bound to that root bone. Now I'm setting up the trunk's position and taper along a gentle vertical curve facing +Z.

I'm placing the seat branch angling upward from the trunk toward the koala's rump, working out how the koala's thighs would rest or straddle it given the lean, and nudging the body's radius so it embeds slightly into the trunk for a natural contact point.

Now I'm shaping the torso as a pear-like sweep from wide hips up through the belly to a narrower chest and neck, defining the spine path and radii at each level to get that rounded koala body silhouette.

I'm figuring out head placement and scale next, trying a big flat wide head sitting close to the shoulders with minimal neck, then checking the overall seated height against the seat position and adjusting the hip, chest, and head y-coordinates downward so the proportions read as a realistically scaled sitting koala.

For the pixel-style rendering, I'm planning the color palette and shading approach: grey fur ramps with a dithered cell-paint technique, cream belly, white ear interiors, black nose, lighter chest tones, white cheek and ear fluff, and mottled brown/white rump patches to mimic real koala coloring. For the head geometry, I'm considering using a flattened sphere primitive to form the ovoid shape.

Deciding on a head joint oriented forward-up, I'm now sketching the skull as a scaled sphere positioned to build out the facial structure.

Adding cheek puffs, a large oval black nose set high on a pale short muzzle, since koalas have that distinctive big nose shape.

Adding the lower jaw and pale muzzle shapes, then working out the eyes — tiny black bead-like pixel eyes placed symmetrically on the skull surface, likely using small textured boxes to get that pixel-art look.

For the facial features, I'm thinking decals could work well since they project directly onto the curved skull surface — using them for eyes, mouth lines, nose highlights, and forehead fur marks, with pixelated texture handled fine by the grid projection. For ears, I'm planning a big round shape with a fluffy white fringe using a stepped circular extrusion with zero thickness.

Positioning the ears on the head's local coordinates, tilted outward with the extrusion axis along x and y slightly offset so the disc faces mostly forward — I need to double check the mirroring works correctly, since flipping the side sign could flip the thickness direction unexpectedly for the opposite ear.

The painting logic uses world normals rather than model-space orientation, so regardless of which way the mesh faces, I can define the ear coloring based on radial distance from the ear center: a soft white fluffy center within some radius, transitioning to grey rim with a darker fringe, and use the normal's z-component to decide which face gets the white fluff versus the grey back — this should correctly handle both ears even when one is mirrored.

I'm sizing the ears around R=0.07 for a whimsical, slightly oversized koala look, and I'm working out the stepped circular outline by computing row half-widths from the radius using a cell size of 0.014, giving roughly ten rows for the silhouette, with the outline centered at the origin so extrusion works cleanly along the correct axis. I'm also thinking through how the ears attach via a hinge joint, and considering whether to add small fur-tuft cards around the rim for extra fluffiness, versus just extruding the ear with a thicker white edge instead.

Now I'm figuring out texel sizing for the fur-tuft cards so they stay pixel-consistent with the rest of the model, settling on something like a 4x4 pixel tuft at roughly 0.016 texel to match the base grid, and planning to scatter a modest number of these across the chest, belly, rump, and forearm backs for texture without blowing the budget.

For the body paint itself, I'm writing a dithered cell shader that bases the fur color on a grey ramp, lightens toward the top using the normal and some noise, carves out a lighter cream chest/belly patch using position checks against the surface coordinates, and adds occasional random darker or lighter flecks for variation.

Now I'm working out the limb rig -- placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints for koala-style gripping arms, and figuring out where the hands should clasp around the trunk's sides based on its radius and height.

I need to pin down the sign convention: +1 for left side using +X, labeling it "L". For elbow hints I'm thinking they should point outward and back.

Now I'm designing the koala's hand with a palm box, two opposed thumbs, and three clawed fingers, curling them as curved tubes wrapping around the trunk's front and back near the hip.

For the grip, I'm reconsidering the hug pose: palms should sit on the front-sides of the trunk at roughly 50° from front, with fingers wrapping toward the back and thumbs curling toward the front, computing palm position using sine/cosine offsets from trunk center.

I'll give each finger a two-joint chain, keeping the hands symmetric for a neutral rest pose rather than a reaching asymmetric one. For the legs, I'm placing the hips, knees, and feet so the hind feet grip the sides of the branch at a fixed height.

Now I'm working out how the feet curl around the branch's cross-section, treating it like the hand grip: toes arc around the branch axis using the same rotation approach as the fingers, wrapping from the top toward the underside.

For the legs themselves, I'm positioning the thighs angling forward and slightly outward from the hips to the knees, then the shins angling back down and inward toward the ankles, so the whole leg straddles the branch naturally in a sitting posture.

Setting the knee hint direction and checking leg segment lengths against the hip-to-ankle distance. Now I'm laying out the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root, with legs parented underneath, and a spine chain of a few joints running from hips up to the neck using interpolated points.

For the head, I'm adding a simple neck joint followed by a head joint pointing forward-up. Then I'm defining a body sweep along the spine path with catmull-rom interpolated points from the hip region up to the neck, assigning radii to shape a pear-like torso profile.

Checking the math: with hips at y=0.62 and a round-cap radius of 0.17, the rump bottom reaches about 0.45, clipping noticeably through the branch top at 0.52. I'll raise the hip position to y=0.66 so the rump bottom lands around 0.50, letting it sink just slightly into the branch for a natural seated look.

Working through the full spine path now — hips at 0.66 rising to chest around 0.86, neck at 0.96, head center at 1.02, ears peaking at 1.17 — giving a total koala height of roughly 0.67, which feels right for a seated adult koala with oversized ears. I'm laying out the body sweep radii along this spine to define the trunk shape.

I realize the hips position needs adjusting forward in z so the rump doesn't collide with the trunk center — shifting hips to z≈0.09 and recalculating the branch/seat position so the rump sinks slightly into the branch surface, then placing the knees and feet further along the branch toward z=0.3-0.33.

For the legs, I'm computing straddling positions with the foot centered near the branch surface and the knee raised above it, then using inverse kinematics with thigh and shin lengths of roughly 0.22 and 0.16 to connect hip to knee to ankle with an upward bend. For the head, I'm placing the skull center slightly forward and up from the head joint to orient it naturally looking ahead.

I'm positioning the arms with shoulders about 0.14 units out from center and computing hand placement at roughly a 50-degree trunk angle, giving upper and lower arm lengths of about 0.15 each bent outward so the koala appears to be clinging, even though the arm segments pass close to the head.

I realize the hands end up tucked behind the head at that height, mostly hidden from a front view, so I'm lowering the hands to around y=0.78 so fingers rest below the chin where the trunk is visible, keeping the gripping pose readable from the front.

For the top of the trunk, I'm planning a fork near y=1.3 into two limbs with leaf clusters, one angling upper-left and one upper-right, plus a trunk tip reaching to about 1.75, giving a total stand height near 1.9. For the eucalyptus leaves I'm designing small lanceolate blue-green cards with a visible midrib using a compact pixel texture, and for the bark I'm layering cream, grey, and greenish-tan ribbons stretched vertically with darker strips to mimic peeling gum bark.

For the bark coloring, I'm choosing shades from a muted ramp based on stretched noise to create vertical streaking peel patches, using a simple hash on column position to vary tint intensity. Then for the base, I'm designing a low-poly cut-log stump with a ring-textured top mimicking wood grain, topped with a thin grass tile layer.

I'm planning scattered details on top of the stump: moss patches, small rocks, flat leaning leaf cards, cup-shaped gumnuts, a tiny mushroom, and grass tufts for texture. For the seat branch, I'm adding bark texture with knots and twig stubs, plus fluffy cream-and-pink pom-pom eucalyptus blossoms with visible stamens for a charming finishing touch.

For the koala itself, I'm mapping out fur painting across body, belly, and rump, then detailing the head with cheek fluff, forehead tufts, muzzle, nose, eyes, and ears with white fringe tufts. I'm also planning the arms and legs with fur sweeps, claws on fingers and toes, a white chest patch in a Y-shape with fur tufts, and elbow tufts, all using consistent cell-painting at a fine texel scale for that soft pixel-art look.

I'm working out texel density for the paint sheet relative to the koala and stand's surface area, settling on a cell size that gives roughly 6 texels per unit for body fur and finer 3-texel cells for small parts like fingers and face, possibly bumping the atlas to 2048 for extra resolution. I'm also sketching tiny pixel-art eye decals, aiming for small black bead eyes with a subtle highlight.

Now I'm sizing the eyes more precisely as a 5x5 highlight pattern around 0.05 wide for a cute, fine texel look, then shifting to designing the nose as a rounded muzzle puff with a separate darker nose box, positioning both using local offsets from the head and scaling the nose fairly wide relative to the face.

Working out joint placement for the skull, neck, and head now—anchoring the head joint near (0, 0.93, 0.15), computing the skull center offset forward and up from it, defining skull radii for front/back/top/bottom extents, and tracing the spine path forward through the chest and hips so the body leans naturally into the neck and head joints.

I'm defining the spine chain using a catmull curve through hip and chest points, naming each segment joint (spine1 through spine3), then parenting a neck joint off the final spine joint to continue the chain upward into the head.

Still structuring the skeleton...

Writing taper and skinning setup...

Then for feet I'm making the tip joint "ankleL" sprout toe chains, each toe parented at the ankle tip with its own small arc chain.

Counting joints: legs come to roughly 22 with their toes, arms to roughly 26 with digits, totaling near 70 which seems reasonable. For the arm chain I'm naming the sequence shoulder, elbow, wrist before branching into fingers.

Now I'm defining the trunk path with control points rising from base to top, and setting up a radius interpolation function so the trunk tapers from about 0.1 at the base down to 0.04 near the top.

At the hand height I'm placing a center point along the trunk and positioning each finger's palm attachment using a radial offset and angle, then working out which direction to rotate each finger around the vertical axis so it curves naturally toward the correct side.

I'm positioning the individual fingers stacked along the y-axis with slight radius tapering toward claw tips, computing each finger's arc path radius as the trunk radius plus a small offset, and now setting up the trunk path function to get exact center coordinates at that height.

Still defining trunk curve...

Now I'm laying out a branch path curving off the trunk at y=0.40, running through a few control points up to a tip around y=0.76, with branch radius tapering from 0.055 down to 0.03.

I'm working out a helper that finds the branch's y-value at a given z by searching for the closest parameter along the path. Then I'm setting up the toe placement by computing a center point and tangent direction on the branch at z=0.33, so the toes can wrap radially around the branch axis in the plane perpendicular to that tangent.

Still writing arc rotation logic...

Now I'm working out where the ankle should sit relative to the toe start point, computing it as the branch center plus radius times the initial direction vector to position the foot joint correctly.

From there, I'm placing the ankle offset outward and upward from that point, treating the foot as clasping the branch with the sole on top and toes wrapping under. Then I'm computing the knee-to-ankle shin segment length and continuing to work out the thigh position from hip to knee.

I'm checking that the thighs sit outside the branch radius without clashing, confirming the trunk and hand contacts look fine, and deciding to simplify by using inverse kinematics for the legs with a bend hint rather than fully specifying sole geometry. Now I'm sketching the foot structure as a pad sphere at the ankle extending to the base of the toes.

For the toes, I'm planning a short rod from the ankle joint to the metatarsal point with claws modeled as thin arcs, plus three toes stacked along offsets perpendicular to the branch wrap and a separate opposable big toe curving the opposite direction, mirroring the same stacked-digit approach I'll use for the hand's fingers and thumb.

For the hand, I'm designing a koala-style grip with two shorter, opposable thumbs curving inward on one side and three longer fingers curving outward on the other, stacking them along the y-axis with slightly varied radii and a wide palm pad as the base.

I'm applying the same logic to feet with a flattened vertical palm capsule and toe digits offset along the foot axis, mimicking a koala's opposable big toe versus fused smaller toes, then connecting ankle to palm with a simple rod, before moving on to placing eucalyptus leaf tufts on extra trunk branches.

Plotting branch paths...

Now I'm thinking through the leaf cards—placing pixel lance-leaf textures along the branch frames using sweep sampling, with each leaf leaning around 50-80 degrees and angled to flow downward like hanging eucalyptus foliage.

I'm designing a tiny pixel-art texture function for the lanceolate leaf shape, computing per-row width using a sine curve profile and shading the midrib lighter with darker/lighter halves on either side.

For other elements, I'm sketching small gumnuts as brown spheres with cone-cap lids, blossoms as clusters of cream and pink-dotted spheres, and a stump base made from a short bark-sided cylinder that the trunk sinks into at its base.

Writing lathe profile...

For the sides I'll use a bark-style paint, while the top gets moss/leaf coloring using noise for green patches. I'm adding small detail extras too: a few low-poly pebbles, mushrooms, flat leaf cards, grass tufts, and maybe a tiny wooden plaque with a paw-print at the base front.

Working out the plaque geometry now — figuring out where it fits against the base's curved surface and sizing a small pixel-art sign with a leaf and paw design, though the base height is tight so I need to scale it down.

I'll make the plaque a thin tilted box with a pixel texture leaning back for readability, sized with a 0.01 texel grid, and apply similar small textures to grass cards. I need to watch part and triangle budgets, so I'll merge geometries for repeated small items like gumnuts and pebbles to keep counts manageable.

Now I'm defining the color palette: cool grey fur ramps, a lighter belly tone, brownish rump tint, dark nose shades, and pale ear-inner colors, keeping everything within a limited flat-color palette.

Rounding out the palette with claw, eye, skin pad, bark, leaf, and wood tones, I'm making sure the total flat colors stay within the 64-color limit before moving into writing the actual rendering code, starting with a pseudo-random hash function for texture noise.

Now I'm defining the fur body paint function, blending noise-based shading with belly/chest highlighting based on surface normals and position to create a natural coat gradient.

For the rump I'm adding a mottled brown patch using threshold noise, plus scattered lighter and darker specks for texture variation, which together with subtle vertical streaking should be enough to sell the fur without needing full directional strokes.

I'm building a shared fur-painting factory that body, limbs, and head all reuse, with limbs getting slightly darker backs. For the head specifically, I'm computing paint based on position relative to the skull center -- white fluff on lower cheeks, pale muzzle toward the front, darker forehead, and cream around the chin.

Now I'm thinking through the facial features: big round white-furred ears, a large black nose, cream muzzle and chin, maybe a dark eye surround via a decal. Before writing the actual file, I want to double-check the API signatures for sticks, decals, and cards in the builder module, plus nail down the head joint's position and orientation so the forward/up/left local coordinate system works correctly for placing these features.

Working through the nose and muzzle placement, I'm adjusting coordinates so the nose sits slightly forward and higher on the face, protruding just past the muzzle sphere's extent.

Still positioning mouth parts...

Now I'm placing the eyes as decals on the skull surface, calculated using azimuth and elevation angles from the skull center, with a pixelated texture applied for that blocky look. Then I'm setting up the ear joints positioned outward and upward from the skull, hinged so they can rotate, with disc shapes forming the ear base.

I'm checking that the ear position falls just outside the skull ellipsoid by verifying the normalized coordinates sum to slightly over one, confirming the ears sit correctly on the surface. Now I'm working out the tilted extrusion plane for the ear discs, defining the local axes so they angle outward by about 25 degrees.

Checking the normal direction confirms sx=1 gives a proper forward-outward facing normal, but sx=-1 flips it to point backward-inward, which breaks the symmetry for painting since the front face logic depends on which side faces positive z.

For ear fluff, I'm planning white fringe cards around the rim with a grey base, using six tufts per ear positioned at points along the rim arc and oriented outward with frames built from each point's direction.

Drafting tuft pixel texture...

For claws and hands, I'm setting up a gradient band system where fur color transitions into a darker claw tone near fingertips, with claw length roughly a quarter of the finger sweep. For the arms, I'm defining a chain of tapering radii from shoulder to wrist with a secondary fur color and smooth joints.

Now I'm placing the palm as a capsule shape with a padded darker tone, positioned radially so the wrist joint aligns with the palm center where the arm chain terminates, letting the elbow come from inverse kinematics. Fingers then branch from the palm's outer edge at an angle, each arcing outward toward the trunk with a defined length and spread.

I'm checking that the finger radius keeps them hugging the trunk without colliding badly with the palm capsule, and placing the thumb at a different angle toward the front so it has clearance in the gap between the hand and the trunk's body contour at that height.

I'm also reconsidering the hip's z-offset so the body curve meets the trunk front more naturally, then computing the shoulder-to-palm vector at the given joint angle to check the resulting limb length and elbow bend direction.

Now I'm skipping a tail stub for the koala and thinking about adding a small decal on the skull for eye detail, using the surface hit point directly so its position and normal align automatically. For the eye texture, I'm deciding whether to mirror the highlight so it stays consistent with the viewer's perspective on both sides.

Since both eyes don't need mirroring, I'll set mirror to false and write a helper to locate surface hits on each skull part. For the leaf geometry, I'm setting up card frames along the branch sweeps with size, lean, flow, bend, and spin parameters, explicitly specifying the root bone since these are standalone sweeps without a bone chain. I'm also planning to merge gumnut and blossom geometries by type and apply bark coloring to the branch sweeps.

Now I'm working out the structural parts of the stand — trunk, seat branch, three main branches, and twigs — plus bark details like knots (flattened dark spheres with a hollow knot decal) and peeling bark strips. For the strips, I'm figuring out how to orient card frames outward from the trunk surface so they curl and hang naturally, adjusting lean and flow values to get a convincing peeled-bark look.

Now I'm defining the base shape as a lathe profile with tiered outline points for the base paint layers.

For surface coloring, I'm deciding the top face treatment: tier2's top could be soil or moss with a green tint, while tier1's rim stays grassy.

Actually I think I'll build this as a layered "earth plinth" in a pixel-art style: dirt brown sides with pebble texture, grassy green tops with a drippy fringe where grass hangs over the edge based on noise, and a stone-textured lower tier near the base.

I'm sketching out a brick pattern for the stone tier using staggered rows, and planning to use Worley cell noise for a mortar effect between stones, with a hash function for pseudo-random grey shading. Writing noise and cell logic...

Now I'm setting up imports for the koala sculpt builder, pulling in geometry merging, path/IK helpers, and the pixel-paint kit for cell shading and bayer dithering. Setting up the builder config and RNG seed, deciding on texel size and paint atlas resolution for the fur texture cells.

I'm defining the skeletal joints next: a root, hips, and a spine chain built from catmull-rom control points running up the back, which I'll sweep into a tapered pear-shaped body profile with a belly bulge partway up and a fur-colored surface.

For the body cross-section I'm tuning radius functions so the rx/ry taper narrows toward the shoulders, placing shoulder joints at roughly x=±0.13-0.14 to match the sides of the torso, keeping the rump bulge large like a koala's. Then I'm adding a neck joint parented off the top spine joint, aiming it upward and slightly forward toward where the head will attach.

Now I'm defining the head joint parented to the neck, oriented facing forward along +Z, and sketching how surface decals on the skull will be positioned using an around/at helper that takes an angle and elevation against a center point. I'm also starting to lay out the leg geometry, defining hip and target points for an IK chain down to the ankle and foot, working from a branch center reference point to compute the rest of the leg's placement.

Using a bend hint with sideways and upward bias to keep knees from collapsing symmetrically, I'll check this in the preview. For the foot, I'm building a tapered rod from the ankle joint to the toe root, then attaching a toe chain as a child with its own curved path.

Still writing toe and finger chain code...

Now I'm defining the trunk shape—path points along its height, curvature functions for x/z offset, and a tapering radius function based on height.

Plotting the branch points for B1 going up-left from the trunk, tapering the radius as it extends, then starting coordinates for B2 branching off higher up the trunk.

Adding a small twig off that branch plus leaves at the trunk tip, then setting up leaf placement by sweeping along each branch with randomized angles and different leaf counts per branch.

Now I'm sizing the leaf cards and estimating total triangle count, which stays manageable even with around a hundred leaves. I'm planning color variance using two different green textures picked randomly per leaf, plus a few blossoms near the second-branch tips and small gumnut clusters built from spheres and caps placed along the branch sweeps.

For ground decoration at the base, I'm scattering pebbles, mushrooms, grass tufts, fallen leaves, and a sign, with flat leaf cards leaning to lie on the ground in random directions and grass tufts scattered around the base ring while avoiding the trunk center.

For the sign, I'm designing a small tilted wooden plaque texture with a tan background, dark brown border, and a simple leaf emblem with dash marks suggesting text, mounted on two small posts positioned to the front-right of the base, tilted back. I also need to check that the branch overhang doesn't extend outside the base radius.

I'm shortening the branch seat to end at z=0.6 and widening the base tiers to radii 0.66 and 0.58 to fix the overhang, repositioning the seat's endpoint accordingly and confirming leaf placement still clears. I'm positioning the sign at the front of the base, leaning back, checking it clears the koala's feet and the branch above, and figuring out the rotation needed to tilt the sign's face upward.

Rotating the box by -50° about X tips the plaque's front face up and forward as intended. I'm defining the small post legs for the sign, then deciding to skip a separate decal for the trunk's hollow knot and instead use a squashed sphere with a dark ring. Writing the bark color palette array...

Still writing bark texture logic...

input.command: cd ~/tmp-archive/sonnet-100/koalaSonnet && grep -n "scale" src/builder.ts | head -20; grep -n "export function limb" -A12 src/ik.ts | head -30; grep -n "interface CardOptions\|type CardOptions" -A25 src/*.ts | head -50
